what_i_did: Read lab/TASKS.md, tasks/planning/spec.md, tasks/planning/dev.json and the checker code in lab/core.py. Wrote 21 single-mode tasks (g2-01..g2-21), each with a different scheduling idea: plain sequence, latest start, relative drying gap, staggered parallel starts, idle time, slack, non-binding window, fixed lunch break, window-forced order, backward plan with passive gap, two parallel chains, repeated slots with gaps, deadline overrun, common free window, critical path, two-machine pipeline, critical path on the clock with an arrival time, latest start over parallel chains, deadline-forced order of four jobs, hands-on vs waiting steps for one cook, work/rest cycle.
verification: Every expected answer is computed in Python by the generator script (clock arithmetic in minutes, a longest-chain function for dependency graphs, a loop for the work/rest cycle) and asserted against the value in the reference. Uniqueness claims were brute-forced over all permutations: g2-09 (1 feasible order of 3), g2-19 (1 feasible order of 4), g2-20 (all 3 valid hands-on orders give 120, 140, 145; 120 also equals the bread-chain lower bound). Negatives are the tempting wrong answer (sum of all durations, ignoring a wait or break, taking the constraint time as the start).
checks: Clock answers: any of exact_any (HH:MM, H:MM, am/pm and bracketed variants) or an anchored ANSWER regex; minute answers: number check.
not_done: Difficulty labels are estimates from the spec's baseline observations; they were not measured on the model.
